newsitem.title: USA: CBOT announces grain task force after CFTC order.
newsitem.headline: CBOT announces grain task force after CFTC order.

text.p: The Chicago Board of Trade announced the formation of a new corn and soybean delivery task force Thursday following an order from the Commodity Futures Trading Commission to resolve the exchange's shortage of grain storage space.

"We were fully aware of the need to increase grain storage capacity in Chicago," said Deborah Kostroun, CBOT spokeswoman. "Chairman Arbor was already planning to form a new delivery task force in January."
The CBOT first formed an 11-member committee in 1995 to examine possible new grain delivery points for the corn and soybean futures contracts.
The committee issued recommendations to expand the number of grain delivery points, but the plan was rejected by the CBOT membership in a vote in October, 1996.
The new task force will be headed by Bill Evans, vice president with commercial firm, Iowa Grain.

In addition to the task force, the CBOT will also form a grain delivery subcommittee that will include representatives from various national trade groups, incluing the National Grain and Feed Association, the National Corn Growers' Association and the American Soybean Association, Kostroun said.
The CFTC said on Thursday that the exchange would have 75 days to resolve its storage capacity problems, or the government agency would formulate its own solution.
Members of the new grain delivery task force are still being selected and no first meeting date has been scheduled.
